criteria.justification: The response explicitly notes that "the problem isn't that we haven't found the right word yet" but rather an "optimization against a moving target," treating round four primarily as a "process decision."
The candidate suggests establishing a "named owner," a "time box," and a strict "reopening rule," while explicitly acknowledging that "the cost of continued churn is real and mostly invisible."

The response limits endless re-litigation by acknowledging that "everything has a flaw" and requiring future objections to prove a name is "worse on the agreed criteria than a specific alternative, not merely that it has a flaw."

The candidate directly factors in the locked API field name, noting that it should be evaluated as a candidate itself and acts as a "strong tiebreaker" since "developers will see it anyway and alignment has real value."

The candidate refuses to generate a new name because a fresh candidate would just have an "unknown failure mode," explicitly choosing to re-evaluate the "existing candidates rather than inventing a fourth."
